architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept transfer of the H-CORE quantitative baseline if the repeat-mean SI_15_60 is between 7.51% and 11.51%, inclusive, corresponding to the 9.51% prediction within the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If repeat-mean SI_15_60 is below 7.51%, H-CORE's E1-derived linear prediction at phi_r = 1.0000 is falsified on its registered low-drift side. If it is above 11.51%, the quantitative 9.51% baseline transfer is also rejected as outside measurement resolution, although this is not evidence for resin suppression. No numerical outcome from this unmodified candidate falsifies or supports H-RESIN or H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run the supplied matched-window M-HOLD-120 protocol as a controlled matched series containing an acrylic-only E2-core formulation and a formulation with the same E2-core proportions and acrylic loading plus a nonzero minor tackifier-like fraction. Use at least two independently prepared repeats per condition, control and record preparation and melt history, and compare each result with 9.51% × phi_r and with half of that linear prediction.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Mean SI_15_60 across at least two independent repeats, where SI_15_60 = 100 × (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 at 120 C.
judge_normalized.rationale: This direct matched-window hold measurement is scientifically defensible as the necessary E2 baseline despite having zero modifier-axis discrimination. It can determine whether the frozen 9.51% core prediction transfers to E2 before modifier effects are interpreted, while avoiding unsupported formulation-level or molecular claims.

planner.failure_mode: Excessive, formulation-dependent viscosity growth during prolonged 120 °C melt residence.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal-hold run showed SI_15_60 = 0.5154, corresponding to a 51.54% viscosity increase from 15 to 60 min at 120 °C; by comparison, E1 increased 9.51% over the same measured window.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have local thermal-hold trajectories, each represented by one measured run at 120 °C over 15–90 min, and no hold trajectory is supplied for the E2 reactive-core anchor or any prospective resin-modified composition. In contrast, temperature response is measured from 80–130 °C for E1, E2, and E3, including multiple E2 runs. Realized viscosity level is uncertain because E2 shows large run spread, but it is at least directly sampled across those runs.
measurement_requirements: Measure the primary mechanistic observable directly with the matched-window 120 °C hold protocol: viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15.
Use at least two independent hold repeats per formulation and preserve the observed viscosity units; do not infer unmeasured values.

Include comparisons that permit the measured drift to be tested against the frozen H-CORE linear-dilution prediction E1_drift × phi_r and the H-RESIN criterion of drift below half that prediction, using the declared 2 percentage-point discrimination threshold.

Include an acrylic-only condition and a composition with a nonzero minor tackifier-like fraction under otherwise comparable reactive-core and acrylic conditions so that tackifier-required suppression under H-DUAL can be separated from general resin suppression.
Record and control preparation and melt-history variables so that hold drift is not confounded with the large realization displacement already observed for E2.

Measure a realized viscosity-level anchor on each tested preparation, preferably at 110 °C with direct 120 and 130 °C checks, so hold-stability conclusions can be interpreted alongside formulation-to-formulation and preparation-to-preparation viscosity displacement.
Keep all temperature and time claims within the measured 80–130 °C and 15–60 min decision windows unless additional measurements explicitly extend support.
planner.scientific_question: At resin-modified compositions based on the E2 reactive core, is 120 °C hold drift consistent with reactive-mass linear dilution, suppressed substantially beyond dilution, or suppressed only when the minor tackifier-like axis is nonzero? The outcome must distinguish H-CORE from H-RESIN and compare acrylic-only with tackifier-containing conditions to test H-DUAL.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: Drift below 4.75% across at least two repeats would falsify the registered H-CORE linear-dilution prediction for the E2 core at phi_r = 1. It would establish that the E1-derived 9.51% baseline does not transfer to E2 as assumed. It would not establish H-RESIN because no resin is present, and it would not test H-DUAL because neither modifier axis is active.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: A result near 9.51% within the 2 percentage-point resolution would support use of the H-CORE linear baseline for the unmodified E2 core. A result at or above 9.51% cannot validly falsify resin suppression at a resin-modified composition because this candidate contains no resin; a substantially higher value would instead show that E1 is not a transferable baseline for E2.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: Drift between 4.75% and 9.51% would indicate partial deviation from the frozen E1-based baseline without meeting the registered superlinear-suppression acceptance threshold. It would refine the E2 baseline but remain unable to attribute the change to acrylic-like or minor-tackifier-like modification.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, during a 120 C hold with viscosity readings at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min across at least two independent repeats.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It has the same component vector and direct hold observable, but it is not the exact E2 center requested by the planner; E1 already has an original hold trajectory, whereas E2 does not.

It is another measured reactive-core composition with identical deterministic value, but its shifted core composition weakens continuity with the designated E2 anchor and does not improve hypothesis separation.
It directly addresses preparation-state variability and lowers process-state risk, but it does not observe the isothermal drift coordinate on which H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL disagree.

proposer.reasoning: The deterministic top set is genuinely tied, but every tied card has zero registered hypothesis-pair discrimination because all are unmodified cores. S1C02 is selected as the scientifically strongest baseline experiment: it directly measures the least-resolved coordinate at the exact E2 anchor, uses the matched 120 C decision window without model fitting or extrapolation, and addresses the missing trajectory needed before interpreting later modifier comparisons. It lies within the characterized local reactive-core family but outside the external modifier intervention regions, so it cannot adjudicate H-RESIN or H-DUAL and should not be represented as doing so.
proposer.tie_break_justification: S1C02 is the measured E2 reactive-core anchor specified by the planner and exactly matches the characterized E2 normalized composition. Unlike the other tied core variants, it fills the explicitly identified missing E2 hold trajectory while allowing direct linkage to E2's existing 80-130 C temperature support and documented realization spread. The measurement is direct and matched to the failure window. However, because no modifier axis is active, all three registered hypotheses predict 9.51% and no hypothesis pair is prospectively separated.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Retain S1C02::M-HOLD-120 only as the E2 baseline arm, not as a standalone hypothesis-adjudication experiment. Expand it into the matched controlled series recommended by the Skeptic: at minimum, add an acrylic-only formulation and a tackifier-containing formulation at matched E2 reactive-core proportions and matched acrylic loading, use at least two independently prepared repeats per condition, and explicitly control and record preparation and melt-history variables. No supplied identifier permits replacing S1C02 with a named modifier candidate.
residual_decision_risk: The weight-perturbation sweep was withheld, so the tied top set's sensitivity and recommendation flip boundaries are unknown.
No candidate IDs or complete experiment cards for the required acrylic-only and tackifier-containing conditions are supplied.
The E2 system has shown up to a 3.5688-fold viscosity spread at 120 C, while M-HOLD-120 does not itself control process state.
The unmodified E2 baseline can test transfer of the E1-derived 9.51% reference but cannot establish or falsify resin-induced suppression or tackifier-required suppression.
External modifier evidence supports only coarse candidate regions and does not establish an exact local formulation or mechanism.
Modifier reactivity and true NCO:OH stoichiometry remain uncertain unless material specifications are verified.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection concerns experiment selection, not merely interpretation. S1C02::M-HOLD-120 activates neither modifier axis and assigns H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL the same 9.51% prediction, so it cannot answer the registered three-way scientific question. It remains useful as the controlled E2 baseline, but it should not be run as the sole adjudicating experiment. The scientifically appropriate design is a matched M-HOLD-120 series containing this E2 baseline, an acrylic-only condition, and a tackifier-containing condition with the same E2 core proportions and acrylic loading, with controlled preparation and melt history. The payload does not provide candidate IDs for those modifier conditions, so a different single candidate_id::measurement_id cannot be named without inventing an identifier.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal is one of nine tied top experiments under the supplied minimality-first deterministic rule order. However, the decision-stability report is explicitly withheld, so top_experiment_set_stability, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, and recommendation_flip_boundary are unavailable. Consequently, no specific weight perturbation that would change the tied top set can be identified, and the scientific defensibility of any such re-weighting cannot be assessed from the payload. Independently of the missing sweep, greater weight on hypothesis discrimination or intervention sufficiency would be scientifically defensible because the stated question requires separating H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL, while every member of the reported tied top set has zero separated hypothesis pairs.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The measurement can attain the numerical H-CORE outcomes because direct SI_15_60 values below 4.75%, within 2 percentage points of 9.51%, or above 9.51% are measurable. It cannot validly attain the stated H-RESIN or H-DUAL falsifications: H-RESIN requires a resin-modified composition, and H-DUAL requires an acrylic-only condition, while S1C02 has 0.0% acrylic-like modifier and 0.0% minor tackifier-like modifier. Thus the composite card-level falsification criterion is not attainable as a valid hypothesis adjudication.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any claim that this experiment adjudicates H-RESIN, H-DUAL, or the requested three-way scientific question would be unsupported; it can only establish an E2-specific unmodified-core hold baseline.
objections.objection: Experiment S1C02::M-HOLD-120 activates neither modifier axis: AC1920 = 0.0% and TK100 = 0.0%, with reactive_mass_fraction = 1.0000. Its own hypothesis_discrimination_detail assigns H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL the identical prediction of 9.51%, yielding zero separated pairs at the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution. It therefore cannot answer the stated scientific question about linear dilution versus resin suppression versus tackifier-required suppression. The proposer correctly declares all three hypotheses under hypotheses_not_separated and claims none under hypotheses_separated.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A deviation of E2 SI_15_60 from 9.51% could reflect preparation or melt-history state rather than failure of the E1-derived reactive-core baseline, weakening even the limited E2-baseline inference. No attribution to acrylic or tackifier mechanisms is available because neither modifier is present.
objections.objection: The composition does not confound the acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like axes because both remain fixed at zero. However, M-HOLD-120 has controls_process_state = false, the selected card reports six missing process fields and process_state_risk = 0.75, and E2 previously showed a 3.5688-fold viscosity spread at 120 C. The protocol merely requires at least two independent repeats and does not specify controlled preparation and melt-history variables, despite the planner's explicit requirement to record and control them.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: None for endpoint interpretability; the limitations arise from hypothesis coverage and process-state control rather than from how SI_15_60 is obtained.
objections.objection: No interpretability defect is present in the primary observable. SI_15_60 is calculated directly from measured eta_15 and eta_60 during the matched 120 C hold; it requires no model fit, extrapolation, or imputation. The 30 and 45 min readings provide trajectory checks without changing the direct status of the primary endpoint.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Results could be incorrectly labeled as falsifying H-RESIN or H-DUAL even though the necessary resin-modified and acrylic-only interventions were never performed.
objections.objection: Only the H-CORE baseline-transfer criterion is operationally attainable: this protocol can directly observe SI_15_60 below 4.75%, near 9.51%, or above it. The card-level falsification criterion is invalid for H-RESIN and H-DUAL. H-RESIN is defined for a resin-modified composition, but S1C02 contains no resin, so drift at or above 9.51% cannot falsify resin suppression. H-DUAL is falsified by an acrylic-only composition reaching low drift, but S1C02 is not acrylic-only; it has AC1920 = 0.0%. The card's phrase 'this acrylic-only composition' is factually inconsistent with its formulation_state. The proposer's outcome_interpretation correctly retracts these two invalid adjudications, but that leaves the registered hypotheses untested.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: An E2 core-specific baseline failure could be misrepresented as evidence for a resin mechanism that the intervention never instantiated and the rheological measurement cannot establish molecularly.
objections.objection: No reliance on an unmeasured target-validation identity or outcome is evident. The scope problem is instead the card-level acceptance statement that drift below 4.75% 'accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.' Because the tested formulation has no resin, such a result would show only that the E1-derived 9.51% baseline does not transfer to the E2 core; it could not establish resin-induced superlinear suppression or the registered encounter-frequency mechanism. The proposer's later outcome_interpretation states this limitation correctly.

skeptic.recommended_change: Retain S1C02 only as a controlled E2 baseline, but add matched M-HOLD-120 conditions comprising at minimum an acrylic-only formulation and a tackifier-containing formulation with the same E2 reactive-core proportions and the same acrylic loading. Include a dilution-matched comparison where needed, use at least two independently prepared repeats per condition, and explicitly control and record all preparation and melt-history variables. Compare each resin-modified result with the frozen 9.51% × phi_r linear prediction using the 2.00 percentage-point resolution and the below-half-linear H-RESIN threshold.
skeptic.strongest_objection: S1C02::M-HOLD-120 gives H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL the same 9.51% prediction because both modifier axes are zero, so it has zero registered hypothesis-pair discrimination and cannot answer the stated scientific question.

tool_trace.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: This must be obtained first to load the upstream material-state structure, shared thermal response, state-calibration evidence, and hold-drift design rules before any candidate or experiment ranking is admissible.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

tool_trace.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
tool_trace.reason: After the state-aware structure is loaded, the evidence-derived E2 anchor and independent acrylic-like and tackifier-like axes are needed to construct mechanistically discriminating experiment cards without treating the candidate lattice as a discovered optimum.

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

tool_trace.name: inspect_formulation
tool_trace.reason: The reactive-core anchor composition and transparent fraction summaries are needed to calculate reactive mass fractions and define matched comparisons without conflating chemistry with process state.

tool_trace.name: get_hold_stability
tool_trace.reason: The complete measured low-drift reference trajectory is needed to freeze the H-CORE linear-dilution baseline over the same time window used for prospective measurements.

tool_trace.name: get_hold_stability
tool_trace.reason: The complete measured high-drift reference trajectory is needed to characterize the established failure mode and compare candidate experiment objectives against the original unstable behavior.

tool_trace.name: get_repeatability_risk
tool_trace.reason: E2 has approximately 2.80–3.57-fold nominal run spread across the measured temperatures, so its detailed repeatability risk is required to specify preparation controls and avoid interpreting one viscosity realization as a formulation property.

tool_trace.name: get_temperature_support
tool_trace.reason: Measured support and response descriptors are needed to keep viscosity anchors within the demonstrated temperature domain and select a defensible state-calibration point.

tool_trace.name: query_external_priors
tool_trace.reason: The supplied external digest contains no acrylic-like entries, so source-level analogue evidence and its limitations are needed before assessing acrylic-axis experiment coverage.

tool_trace.name: query_external_priors
tool_trace.reason: The supplied external digest contains no minor-tackifier-like entries, so source-level evidence is needed to assess the sparse local basis for a tackifier-required mechanistic comparison.

voi_sent_to_model.note: The deterministic decision policy for this run is the stated rule ORDER. Experiments are presented in that order. Component vectors are unchanged facts.
voi_sent_to_model.order_description: perturbation size is minimized before intervention sufficiency is assessed

top_cards_in_policy_order.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 4.75% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 9.51% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 1.0000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards_in_policy_order.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 9.51%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 4.75%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. H-DUAL is falsified if this acrylic-only composition reaches the low-drift regime with no minor tackifier present.

measurement_plan.name: matched-window 120 C thermal hold
measurement_plan.protocol: Hold the melt at 120 C. Record viscosity at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min. Report the 15-60 min matched-window relative change. Run at least two independent repeats.
